austrian.fact: US natural gas output is forecast to grow this year by more than the EU's entire production, with Appalachian spot prices around $1-2 per million BTU, and EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in a $13 billion all-stock deal. Gas turbines are sold out for years, some until 2030 or later.

mainstream.claude: The AGOA hit is small next to crime and unemployment, which drive this vote. A lost Johannesburg would still shake the national coalition more than any US tariff.
mainstream.fact: South Africans vote today in local elections where polls put the ANC as low as 32%, and it could lose Johannesburg to the Democratic Alliance. Pretoria played down its removal from the US AGOA trade deal: exports already face a 12.5% US tariff, and losing duty-free access adds about 3.4 percentage points, the agriculture envoy Wandile Sihlobo told Semafor.

thread.text: Democrats won both chambers; Trump congratulated them and pledged to work across the aisle.
thread.title: US midterms

top.claude: The Senate result matters more than the House: without it Trump cannot confirm judges or cabinet members, which turns the next two years into a fight over executive orders and courts. Inflation and fuel prices after the Iran war, not ideology, look like the main driver.
top.fact: Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate in Tuesday's US midterms, Semafor and International Intrigue report, with Senate wins in Texas and Kansas, a Republican seat since 1932, and Maine's Susan Collins ousted. International Intrigue puts the House majority on track for up to 255 seats and the Senate at about 55, while Democrats also won governorships in Texas, Georgia and Iowa. House leaders say they will focus on corruption investigations and the cost of living, and Trump has congratulated the winners and pledged to work across the aisle.

opinion.text: called it a generational wipeout that could leave the party in the Senate minority for years.

top.claude: Watch Iran first: Trump had promised no strikes before the vote, and the reason to hold back is now gone. Europe's lever is that a president without Congress needs foreign wins more, not less.
top.fact: With his domestic agenda blocked, Trump is expected to focus on foreign policy, Semafor reports; he told the Financial Times he has no immediate plans to strike Iran. European officials fear more pressure on trade and defence and uncertainty over Ukraine. On election day Trump also said he had agreed with Netanyahu to wind down the $4 billion a year in US military aid to Israel by the end of the year, two years early.

top.claude: Texas is due to host a large share of new US data-center capacity, so a local political brake is a bigger risk to AI capex than any Washington bill. Rising debt plus less political goodwill is a combination to watch in tech earnings.
top.fact: Stocks and Treasuries gained after the results on hopes that divided government slows US borrowing, Semafor reports, after Nasdaq 100 futures had fallen about 2% overnight as results came in, according to International Intrigue. Tesla and SpaceX slipped after Elon Musk spent heavily against Democrats in Texas, where the new Democratic governor's win suggests a pause on rural AI data centers may now last. Meta launched its first euro bond, and Nikkei estimates Big Tech's off-balance-sheet AI obligations have doubled in six months to about $3.2 trillion.

opinion.text: markets like gridlock; they don't like a party with too much power.
